title: Microsoft Teams: app centric management of app access in the Teams admin center for DoD
summary: The briefing agrees with the roadmap and Microsoft's documented controls, migration behavior and licensing requirements. Its warning about access widening during migration is supported, and its DoD-specific documentation gaps remain appropriately qualified.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026, presented as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; title; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: This roadmap item covers DoD only.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["DoD"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap says admins can set a default for new apps published to the Teams app store.
claims.quote: First, admins can set a default value for new apps that are published to Teams app store.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists All users can install, Specific users and groups can install, and No user can install as app availability choices.
claims.quote: Second, admins can edit the availability of an app to “All users can install,” “Specific users and groups can install,” or “No user can install.”

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the feature as evolving existing app permission policies.
claims.quote: This feature evolves the existing app permission policies and provides admins with the ability to manage access to the app individually.

claims.claim: The roadmap says existing customers' permission policies are migrated to maintain existing app availability.
claims.quote: The app permission policies for existing customers are migrated to maintain existing app availability in the tenant.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 527830 describes the same feature for GCC.
claims.quote: "id": 527830; "title": "Microsoft Teams: App centric management in Teams Admin Center to manage the Apps access for tenants, end-users, and groups in GCC"

claims.claim: The GCC item is Launched.
claims.quote: Item 527830: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The GCC item's target is January CY2026.
claims.quote: Item 527830: "targetDate": "January CY2026"

claims.claim: Roadmap item 569433 describes the same feature for GCC High.
claims.quote: "id": 569433; "title": "Microsoft Teams: App centric management in Teams Admin Center to manage the Apps access for tenants, end-users, and groups in GCC High"

claims.claim: The GCC High item is Rolling out.
claims.quote: Item 569433: "status": "Rolling out"

claims.claim: The GCC High item's target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: Item 569433: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: App centric management controls app access individually in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: This functionality lets you specify which users and groups can use each app or a copilot agent and you can control it on a per-app basis.

claims.where: What's changing, second paragraph; Why it matters
claims.claim: Each app contains an access definition consisting of assigned users and groups.
claims.quote: Each app contains its access definition using a list of users and groups that you assign to it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Everyone availability option covers organization users, new users and guests.
claims.quote: `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Specific users or groups restricts use to selected users and groups and excludes guests even when assigned.
claims.quote: Only the users and groups that you select can use the app. The supported group types are security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups, and the distribution lists. Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The No one availability option makes an app unavailable to any user.
claims.quote: `No one` | Not available to any user | Same as a blocked app.

claims.claim: Supported groups include security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups and distribution lists.
claims.quote: The supported group types are security groups, Microsoft 365 groups, dynamic user membership groups, nested groups, and the distribution lists.

claims.claim: The app centric management Learn page does not specify DoD-specific behavior.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" "DoD" rollout timeline; read the full app-centric-management article and manage-apps article. The former gives general behavior without naming DoD; the latter separately states the government third-party app default.

claims.claim: All third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCCH and DoD Teams deployments.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: Before app centric management, the org-wide third-party app setting controlled third-party availability at organization level.
claims.quote: Org-wide app setting for third-party apps: It applies at an org-level and controls if all third-party apps are available for every user or not.

claims.claim: Before app centric management, app allow/block status controlled availability at app level.
claims.quote: App status: It applies at an app-level as allow or block and controls if it's available to any user or not.

claims.claim: Before app centric management, permission policies controlled app access at user level.
claims.quote: Permission policy: It applies at a user-level and controls if a specific user is allowed to use an app or not.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: After switching to app centric management, organizations cannot access, edit or use permission policies.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.claim: Migration to app centric management cannot be reverted.
claims.quote: Once your organization migrates, you can't revert the migration.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default state is on because Microsoft describes automatic migration without administrator intervention.
claims.quote: Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management.

claims.claim: Existing organizations' old settings map to new access settings.
claims.quote: For existing organizations, old settings are mapped to new access settings.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn documents that an app allowed globally but blocked by a custom policy becomes available to all tenant users during automatic migration.
claims.quote: There's no change of app permissions during the migration, except where an app is allowed in the global policy but blocked in the custom app permission policy. Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant, except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: For EDU customers the documented migration conflict instead makes the app available to none.
claims.quote: Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant, except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: Automatic migration creates one security group per custom app permission policy.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.claim: Users assigned to each app permission policy are added to its corresponding security group.
claims.quote: All users currently assigned to an app permission policy are then added to the corresponding security group for that policy.

claims.claim: The created groups are assigned to the apps their policies allowed, making group membership a determinant of access.
claims.quote: These groups are assigned to each app they're allowed in their respective policy, maintaining their app access. Administrators manage these groups like any others to customize the app centric management assignments

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: App availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to reach the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Teams admin center cannot update app availability in bulk.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: PowerShell Update-M365TeamsApp can be used for bulk availability updates.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell. For more information on PowerShell cmdlets for app availability, see [Update-M365TeamsApp]

claims.claim: Up to 99 users or groups can be added to an app at a time.
claims.quote: You can add up to 99 users or groups at a time to an app.

claims.claim: Learn describes no new autonomous behavior for this access-management change.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" "autonomous". Read app-centric-management and manage-apps; the documented change controls access and availability, with no autonomous behavior described.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each organization user needs a Teams license before using Teams.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: Joining Teams meetings anonymously is an exception to the Teams license requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the product's Teams license requirement, with no feature-specific entitlement asserted.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate license, meter, price or charge is documented for app centric management at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" license subscription pricing; "app centric management" "DoD" licensing price meter. Read app-centric-management, user-access, manage-apps and purchase-third-party-apps; no separate feature entitlement or charge found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No DoD-specific app centric management licensing statement is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "app centric management" "DoD" license. Read app-centric-management, user-access and manage-apps; the product license page names a Teams DoD service plan but no DoD-specific entitlement for this management feature.

claims.claim: Paid third-party apps can require their own publisher service subscriptions, separate from access management.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.

claims.claim: The Learn page says the feature is not available to all organizations.
claims.quote: All organizations don't have the app centric management feature available.

claims.where: Scope: Clouds and rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn directs readers to MC688930 and roadmap item 151829 for timelines.
claims.quote: For timelines, see [Message Center post MC688930](https://admin.microsoft.com/Adminportal/Home#/MessageCenter/:/messages/MC688930) or [Microsoft 365 roadmap item 151829]

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The app centric management Learn page gives no DoD-specific rollout window.
claims.quote: Searched: "app centric management" "DoD" rollout timeline. Read the full app-centric-management article; it gives general migration guidance and timeline pointers, but no DoD-specific window. The briefing separately reports the roadmap's November CY2026 target.

claims.claim: Learn requires the Teams Administrator role to use the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role.

claims.claim: Some higher-privilege administrators can also perform agent and app governance tasks.
claims.quote: Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Previously granted administrator consent to app permissions survives migration.
claims.quote: After migration, any admin consent to app permissions that was previously granted is retained.

claims.claim: App permissions differ from the permission policies replaced by app centric management.
claims.quote: App permissions are a different concept from permission policies, which app centric management is replacing.

claims.claim: The per-app availability path is Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to.
claims.quote:
Select the **Users and groups** tab.
4. Under **Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization**, select **Availability**.
5. Select **Edit availability**.
6. Select the required option from **Available to** menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets the identified app's availability to Everyone.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
```

Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: The AppAssignmentType parameter also accepts UsersAndGroups and Noone.
claims.quote:
### -AppAssignmentType

App availability type.

#### Parameter sets

 (Everyone ... UsersandGroups ... Noone)

claims.claim: OperationType, Users and Groups support adding or removing app assignments.
claims.quote: -OperationType: Operation performed on the app assigment. ... -Users: List of all the users for whom the app is enabled or disabled. ... -Groups: List of all the groups for whom the app is enabled or disabled.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings are reached through Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings.
claims.quote: To change this default setting, access [Manage apps](https://admin.teams.microsoft.com/policies/manage-apps) page, select **Actions** > **Org-wide app settings**, and modify the required settings.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings have separate controls for Microsoft, third-party and custom apps.
claims.quote: Under **Microsoft apps**, a single control ... Under **Third-party apps**, a single control manages the bulk availability ... Under **Custom apps**, turn off or turn on **Let users install and use available apps by default** option.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings govern default availability for new apps in the Teams app store.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings apply to:

- All the new apps made available in Teams app store.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings also govern existing apps whose availability has not been actively managed.
claims.quote: All the existing apps that you didn't actively manage, that is, you didn't change the availability of.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not override individually saved Specific users or groups assignments.
claims.quote:
The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to:

- All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not override individually saved Everyone assignments.
claims.quote: All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not override individually saved No one assignments.
claims.quote: All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not apply to blocked apps.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: ... Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not map a documented automation call to the new Org-wide app settings default-availability toggles.
claims.quote: Searched: "Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings" "DefaultApp" "GlobalApp" "PrivateApp" org-wide; "app centric management" "org-wide" API PowerShell default availability. Read its reference, app-centric-management and manage-apps; no toggle mapping found.

claims.claim: Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings documents the setting names DefaultApp, GlobalApp and PrivateApp.
claims.quote:
### -SettingName

Setting Name to be changed.

#### Parameter sets

 (DefaultApp ... GlobalApp ... PrivateApp ... EnableCopilotExtensibility)

claims.claim: The Manage apps page shows an Available to column for checking app availability.
claims.quote: After migration, your blocked apps continue to remain unavailable to users. The statuses of such apps show as `unblocked` now, but the apps are assigned to `No one` in the `Available to` column on the Manage apps page.

claims.claim: Organizations use permission policies or app centric management rather than continuing to use permission policies after migration.
claims.quote: After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Low cost reflects the documented administrative work rather than a separately documented charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Take inventory of the apps in the permission policies and identify the users and groups that the apps are allowed or blocked for. During the migration, you might have to manually edit the availability for some apps for the existing users and groups.
